requirement.comment: Detection.md entry 14 and The exact requirement prefix selects the type; the lexer reads requirementDiagram case-insensitively and not followed by an ASCII word character, so requirementdiagram is also a header. A newline unit must follow it, with only comments, directives or empty description blocks before it. Follows requirement.md#detection.

patterns.comment: Try TB, BT, RL and LR in that order, before every rule but rules 1 to 4. Those rules read no leading indentation, so an indented accessibility-looking line is a direction line; an unindented accessibility form keeps precedence. Directives inside direction-text join its parts, and directives may lie in the gap before the direction value. Value scopes and text runs end before a separator-led common comment; the enclosing context reads that comment independently. Follows requirement.md#the-statement-context and common.md#comment-lines.

AccDescr, zero or more common whitespace characters, an opening brace, and text through the first closing brace form a description block; braces do not nest. Common directives may lie between the keyword and brace. Retain this local context: reads Notation whitespace after the delimiter with the delimiter and keeps inline percent pairs; its keywords are case-insensitive. Value scopes and text runs end before a separator-led common comment; the enclosing context reads that comment independently. Follows requirement.md#accessibility-values and common.md#comment-lines.
Description block text runs to the first closing brace; quotes are ordinary text. A common comment is trivia in every context. Follows requirement.md#accessibility-values and common.md#comment-lines.

AccTitle and accDescr enter their line-value contexts after the colon and common whitespace; each reads the rest of its line as text. Common directives may lie between the keyword and colon. Retain this local context: reads Notation whitespace after the delimiter with the delimiter and keeps inline percent pairs; its keywords are case-insensitive. Value scopes and text runs end before a separator-led common comment; the enclosing context reads that comment independently. Follows requirement.md#accessibility-values and common.md#comment-lines.

Bounded style, classDef and class enter a context lasting through the line feed, where ASCII word characters and strings are values, and colon, comma, semicolon, dash and hash have style-unit meanings. Value scopes and text runs end before a separator-led common comment; the enclosing context reads that comment independently. The keyword boundary reads through following directives. Follows requirement.md#the-style-context.

patterns.comment: Rule 15: The bounded case-insensitive keywords are id, text, risk, verifyMethod; the six requirement kinds; low, medium, high; analysis, demonstration, inspection, test; element; contains, copies, derives, satisfies, verifies, refines, traces; type and docref. The keyword boundary reads through following directives. Follows requirement.md#the-statement-context.

patterns.comment: Double quotes enclose text other than double quotes, without escapes; an empty string is rejected. Follows requirement.md#units-and-contexts.
A relationship is name, dash, relation, right arrow, name; or name, left arrow, relation, dash, name; whitespace is optional. Follows requirement.md#relationships.

patterns.comment: Rules 11, 12 and 14: Opening brace, closing brace and colon are units of their characters. Follows requirement.md#the-statement-context.

An ASCII word character starts unquoted text that takes as many characters as possible other than colon, comma, line feed, opening brace, angle brackets, dash and equals; keyword-like words, quotes, hash, percent and closing braces inside it remain text. Value scopes and text runs end before a separator-led common comment; the enclosing context reads that comment independently. Follows requirement.md#units-and-contexts and common.md#comment-lines.

requirement-comma.comment: Rule 10 and rule 24: A comma is a comma unit in either context. Follows requirement.md#the-style-context.

requirement-type-field.comment: Read an element's type field as a keyword, colon and text or string value. Follows requirement.md#elements.

patterns.comment: Read the element field value as retained text. Follows requirement.md#elements.

requirement-field.comment: Read a field key and its value. Follows requirement.md#the-statement-context and requirement.md#units-and-contexts.

patterns.comment: Read the field's unquoted text value. Follows requirement.md#units-and-contexts.

requirement-body.comment: Read a requirement or element body, keeping its empty description blocks as ignored text. Follows requirement.md#requirements.

Read the complete fixed-value field so a following empty block remains an ignored body item. Follows requirement.md#requirements.

requirement-comments.comment: At a unit start in the statement context a hash or percent begins a comment through the physical line end; neither starts a comment inside unquoted text, a string or style context. Directives in comment text are read whole. Value scopes and text runs end before a separator-led common comment; the enclosing context reads that comment independently. Follows requirement.md#comments.

patterns.name: comment.line.number-sign.mermaid
patterns.comment: A hash starts a native comment; makes separator-led common comments independent trivia. Follows requirement.md#comments.

patterns.name: comment.line.percentage.mermaid
patterns.comment: A percent starts a native comment; reads directives in its body whole. Neither character of a percent pair belongs to a directive; a lone text percent before a directive keeps the single-percent mark. Follows requirement.md#comments.

requirement-field-value.comment: Read the common parts of field values before the field-specific unquoted text. Follows requirement.md#units-and-contexts.

patterns.name: constant.language.mermaid
patterns.comment: Read a listed risk or verification method. Follows requirement.md#the-statement-context.

requirement-field-header.comment: Read the field keyword, its colon and their directive-bearing gaps once for text and type fields. Follows requirement.md#the-statement-context.
